newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Core members of the six coalition parties are to meet Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa today and are expected to press him to agree to surrender the premiership to New Aspiration Party leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Banharn said to disagree with Chavalit as next premier. He wants to name a candidate from his own Chart Thai party. Chart Thai source said Banharn would not resign until he agrees on his successor (THE NATION).

- Immigration police are targetting illegal immigrants from some African and Asian countries in their continuing crackdown on foreign gangs which indulge in criminal activities on Thai soil. Over the last three months, Immigration Department police have arrested more than 1,000 illegal immigrants as part of an anti-crime drive. (THE NATION)

- The Meteorological Department has issued a warning of possible flash floods in the upper Northeast as tropical storm Willie is expected to hit the region this evening or early tomorrow. (BANGKOK POST)

- Banharn's departure will help markets in the short term. Business leaders welcomes Banharn Silpa-archa's plan to resign as premier, but are guarded about whether the change will revive the country's sluggish economy in the long run. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai rice exporters are worried a delay in approval of importers' licences will adversely affect duty-free and low-tariff sales to the European Union. Thailand has received quotas to export 21,455 tons of white rice exempt from the tariff of 611 European Currency Units. (BANGKOK POST)

- Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand is rushing to sign a memorandum of understanding with financial institutions for an 8.5 billion baht loan for Don Muang Tollway project as the change of government leadership may affect the plan. (THE NATION)
